newsitem.title: UK: British homeowners more confident of price rises.
newsitem.headline: British homeowners more confident of price rises.

text.p: British homeowners, who saw the value of their homes fall during the early 1990s, are now increasingly optimistic they will rise in value, according to research by Barclays Mortgages.
The number of householders who expect house prices to rise has increased by 44 percent since the beginning of the year.
More than half those surveyed, 51 per cent, now believe the value of their homes will increase over the next 12 months, compared with 36 percent at the beginning of 1996.
Some 35 percent of homeowners believed prices will stay the same, while only six percent expected a fall, compared with 48 and nine percent, respectively, at the start of the year.
More people are also likely to move house in the next 12 months, a 17 per cent increase since the first quarter of 1996, Barclays said.
People in London and the South East are the most optimistic about house prices, with 64 percent believing their homes will increase in value in 1997.
The likelihood of moving house in 1997 is also strongest in London and the South East, with 20 percent of those surveyed expressing an intention to move.

"This bodes well for the New Year. It's reassuring to see predictions for housing market recovery coming from those with the power to make it happen - actual homebuyers, that is," said Jim Chadwick, marketing director of Barclays Mortgages.

"Although returning confidence among consumers is most welcome, their cautious optimism far from suggests that boom conditions could be in store. This backs up the findings of the Barclays Mortgage Index, which shows mortgage lending up almost a quarter over the past year."
Barclays Mortgages research covers about 1,000 consumers a month.
